info.title: Relic sync API
info.summary: The HTTP contract between Relic clients and a Relic sync server (Relic Cloud or a self-hosted server).
info.description:
Relic is an open-source, end-to-end encrypted vault for everything you copy. This is the API its apps use to sync. It is written for people building a client or running their own server.

What the server can and cannot do:

- Every relic and blob arrives already encrypted on the device. The server stores ciphertext, enforces quotas and ordering, and never holds a key.
- Every route except `/health`, `/stripe/plans`, `/stripe/webhook`, and the public share views needs a bearer token (see Security). There is no API key you can request; a token comes from signing in to an account or from pairing a device.
- Because the payloads are ciphertext, this is not a data API a third party can read from. It is the sync contract, published so clients and self-hosters can be built against it.

The long-form contract with the reasoning behind each route is docs/api.md (https://relic.space/docs/api.md). The envelope and blob byte formats are docs/wire-format.md; the key derivation and sealing are docs/crypto.md. Relic's website has a separate, account-less one-time note API at relic.space/api/note that is not part of this document.

Source: https://github.com/RelicSync/relic (worker/src). This file lives at docs/openapi.json in that repo and is served at https://relic.space/openapi.json.

servers.description: A self-hosted server on its default port (selfhost/README.md)

tags.name: keyparams
tags.description: The per-account key-params record: the Argon2id salt and parameters plus the wrapped master key. Recovering the master key from it needs the passphrase.

tags.name: relics
tags.description: Encrypted relic envelopes. Last writer wins on `updated_at`; deletes are tombstoned so an offline device cannot bring an item back.

tags.name: blobs
tags.description: Encrypted blob bytes for image and file relics. Plain upload up to 64 MiB, chunked upload past that.

tags.name: ai
tags.description: Sealed AI records (a generated title and tags) and the short work lease that keeps two devices from generating the same one.

tags.name: account
tags.description: Usage, quotas, the device list, and account deletion.

tags.name: pairing
tags.description: The zero-knowledge relay behind the QR join flow. It stores opaque sealed blobs for two minutes and never sees a secret.

tags.name: shares
tags.description: End-to-end encrypted one-way share links. The key travels in the URL fragment and never reaches the server.

tags.name: billing
tags.description: Stripe checkout and portal. Self-hosted servers answer 503 here.

get.description: 200 when the router is up and the database answers. Public, rate-limited per IP.
Every new device fetches this, derives the key-encryption key from the passphrase and the salt, and unwraps the master key. Unwrap failure means a wrong passphrase.

put.description: The first write succeeds. A later write needs `?replace=1` (a passphrase change re-wraps the master key). The body is stored as sent.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: Set to `1` to overwrite an existing record.

409.description: A record already exists and `replace=1` was not given (`keyparams_exists`).

put.description: Last writer wins: if the stored `updated_at` is at or past the envelope's, the write is a no-op and the reply says `stale: true`. A uid with a live tombstone is also `stale: true`, so an offline device cannot resurrect a deleted item. Enforces the per-item size cap (413), the storage quota (402 `storage_quota`), and on free accounts the vault cap when the write newly promotes an item (402 `vault_cap`). On free accounts, unpromoted items past the history ring (500) are pushed out of view after the write.

delete.description: Removes the envelope and its blob, writes a tombstone, and updates the usage counters. Idempotent: deleting a uid that does not exist is still 200.

parameters.name: deleted_at
parameters.description: Unix seconds to stamp on the tombstone. Defaults to now.

get.summary: List envelopes changed since a point in time
get.description: Envelopes with `updated_at` after `since`, oldest first, paginated. Initial sync: `since=0` and page until `next_cursor` is null. Steady state: pass the cursor you saved. On free accounts, items the history ring has pushed out of view are not returned; they come back on an upgrade.

get.summary: List deletions since a point in time
get.description: Up to 1000 tombstones with `deleted_at` after `since`, oldest first. Tombstones are kept for 90 days; a device offline longer than that should do a full resync instead of trusting this feed.

post.summary: Upload an encrypted blob in one request
post.description: Body is the raw sealed bytes (24-byte nonce followed by the ciphertext). The client mints `id` before uploading because the encryption binds it. Use this up to 64 MiB; use the chunked routes past that. Upload the blob first, then push the envelope that references it. A blob no envelope references is swept after 24 hours.

get.description: Raw sealed bytes, resolved inside the token's account only. Served with `Cache-Control: private, immutable`.

post.description: Checks the declared size against the per-item cap and the storage quota before any bytes move, so a client can show its upgrade prompt first. The declared bytes are reserved until the upload completes or is aborted.

put.description: Every part is exactly `part_size` bytes except the last. Parts are numbered from 1.

200.description: Part stored. Keep the etag for the complete call.

post.description: Assembles the parts and re-checks the real size against the cap and the quota. An object over either is deleted and the call fails.

200.description: Stored. Same shape as a plain upload.

get.summary: List AI records changed since a point in time
get.description: Same paging as `/relics`, on the records' own `ai_at` timeline so generated titles never disturb relic ordering.

post.summary: Claim a lease on items to enrich
post.description: One device wins a ten-minute lease per uid; the others skip it. Needs `X-Relic-Device`. Up to 64 items per call. Items in neither `granted` nor `done` are leased by a live peer and may be offered again later.

post.summary: Give back leases this device will not use
post.description: Optional: every lease expires on its own. Needs `X-Relic-Device`.

put.description: Not last writer wins. A higher `level` always wins; at equal level the earliest result stands, and a device may amend its own record. A losing write is `stale: true`, which is not an error. The sealed payload is capped at 48 KiB.

200.description: Written, or ignored because another result stands.

get.description: For the client's quota display. Never includes key material. `history_cap` is null on paid tiers, which is how a client knows there is no ring to warn about.

delete.summary: Delete the account and everything in it
delete.description: Irreversible. Cancels billing, deletes every stored object and row, and removes the sign-in identity. Needs a sign-in token issued within the last ten minutes (`403 stale_token` otherwise), so a leaked bearer alone cannot destroy an account. Clients refresh right before calling.

403.description: The token is too old for this action (`stale_token`). Refresh and retry.

post.description: Enforces the tier's device cap. At the cap the reply is a 409 that carries the current device list, so a client can offer to remove one.

409.description: Device limit reached (`device_cap`). The body includes the current devices.

delete.summary: Remove a device and sign the account out everywhere
delete.description: Revokes every refresh token at the identity provider and refuses access tokens issued before the removal. The provider has no per-session revocation, so every device has to sign in again. `sessions_revoked` says whether that revocation actually happened.

post.description: The channel key is generated on the device and travels only in the QR code. The server just mints the id.

post.summary: Drop a sealed blob into a pairing slot
post.description: Slots: `np` and `tp` (sealed ephemeral public keys, one per side) and `mk` (the sealed master key). Each slot lives for two minutes.

get.summary: Read a pairing slot without consuming it
get.description: Absent, expired, and consumed slots all answer 204, on purpose.

get.summary: Read a pairing slot and delete it
get.description: Single use. Absent, expired, and consumed slots all answer 204.

200.description: The blob. It is gone after this reply.

post.description: The body is the sealed payload (AES-GCM, 12-byte IV, then ciphertext, then the 16-byte tag). The client mints the 22-character id so the encryption can bind to it. The decryption key goes in the URL fragment, which never reaches the server. Per-tier limits apply to how many shares can be live at once and how large one can be.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Client-minted share id: 16 random bytes as unpadded base64url.

parameters.name: ttl
parameters.description: Lifetime in seconds: one hour, one day, or seven days.

parameters.name: views
parameters.description: Maximum number of reveals, 1 to 100. Omit for unlimited within the lifetime.

402.description: Too many live shares for this tier (`share_cap`).

409.description: The id already exists (`share_id_collision`). Mint a new one and retry.

delete.summary: Revoke a share link you created

get.summary: Fetch a share's ciphertext (counts as a view)
get.description: Public. The share page calls this when the recipient clicks Reveal; only this fetch counts a view, so link-preview bots cannot burn a one-time share. Rate-limited per IP.

200.description: The sealed bytes, `Content-Disposition: attachment`, never cached.

410.description: Expired, revoked, or already viewed the allowed number of times (`share_gone`).

get.summary: The recipient page for a share link
get.description: Public HTML, self-contained, `noindex`. Decrypts in the browser with the key from the fragment. Never touches the view count. Rate-limited per IP.

404.description: No such share, or it is gone. Still an HTML page.

get.description: Public. Price ids, tiers, intervals, and amounts, so a client can render an upgrade screen without hardcoding price ids. Cached for five minutes. A server with no billing configured returns an empty list.

200.description: Send the user to this URL.
Send the user to this URL.

409.description: The account has no subscription to manage (`no_subscription`).

post.description: Called by Stripe, not by clients. Authenticated by the `Stripe-Signature` header. Events are applied idempotently.

503.description: Billing is not configured on this server.

get.description: Send `Upgrade: websocket` with the bearer token. The server rings every other device on the account when a write lands; the message carries no content, and the client answers it with a normal pull. A self-hosted server without the feature answers 501 and the client falls back to polling.

501.description: Live sync is not enabled on this server (`no_socket`). Poll instead.

bearerAuth.description: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Two kinds of token are accepted: the access token from signing in to a Relic account (a JWT), and a device token from pairing (an opaque string, used by older installs and the CLI). Relic Cloud issues these through the apps; there is no way to request one over this API. A self-hosted server enrolls devices from the vault passphrase alone. Devices also send `X-Relic-Device` so a removed device can be cut off before its token expires.

XRelicDevice.name: X-Relic-Device
XRelicDevice.description: This device's id (up to 64 characters). Required for the AI lease routes, recommended everywhere: it is how the server skips echoing a write back to its author and how a removed device is cut off early.

uid.name: uid
uid.description: The relic's id, minted by the client.

blobId.name: id
blobId.description: The blob id, minted by the client before encryption.

blobIdQuery.name: id
blobIdQuery.description: The blob id, minted by the client before encryption. 8 to 64 characters of letters, digits, and dashes.

since.name: since
since.description: Unix seconds. Only records changed after this are returned. Defaults to 0.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, unknown, or revoked token (`unauthorized`), a token from before a device removal (`session_revoked`), or a removed device (`device_revoked`). Sign in again.

EmailUnverified.description: Only when the server runs with the verify-to-sync gate on: the account's email is not confirmed yet (`email_unverified`). Reads still work.

QuotaExceeded.description: Over the tier's storage quota (`storage_quota`) or, on free accounts, the promoted-item cap (`vault_cap`).

TooLarge.description: Over the tier's per-item size cap (`too_large`).

RateLimited.description: Too many requests (`rate_limited`). Back off and retry.

Unconfigured.description: This server has no pairing relay (`unconfigured`).

BillingUnconfigured.description: This server has no billing (`billing_unconfigured`). Every self-hosted server answers this.

message.description: Human text. Do not match on it.

stale.description: true means the write was ignored because a newer or winning record already stands. Treat it as done.

KeyParams.description: Stored and returned as sent. Safe to hold server-side: the master key inside is wrapped under a key derived from the passphrase.

Envelope.description: One encrypted relic. The plaintext fields are the minimum the server needs to enforce quotas and ordering; everything about the item is inside `ct`.

uid.description: Must equal the uid in the path.

updated_at.description: Unix seconds. Last writer wins on this.

byte_size.description: The item's plaintext size, charged against the storage quota.

promoted.description: Kept in the vault (exempt from the free history ring).

blob_key.description: The blob this relic references, if any. Omitted for text.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor`. Null on the last page.

key.description: The blob id you sent. Put it in the envelope's `blob_key`.

declared_size.description: The total size you are about to upload, in bytes.

max_parts.description: How many parts the tier's cap allows.

AiRecord.description: A sealed generated title and tags for one relic.

ai_at.description: Unix seconds the result was produced.

level.description: The enrichment level of the models that produced it. Higher wins.

device.description: Which device produced it. Set by the server on reads.

ct.description: The sealed payload, base64, at most 48 KiB.

level.description: The level this device can produce.

granted.description: Uids this device now holds a lease on.

done.description: Uids that already have a result at this level or higher. Stop asking.

lease_expires_at.description: Unix seconds. Zero when nothing was requested.

history_cap.description: The free history ring. Null on paid tiers.

evicted_count.description: Older copies held back by the ring that come straight back on an upgrade. Always 0 on paid tiers.

objects.description: How many stored objects were removed.

last_seen_at.description: Unix seconds, moved at most hourly.

this_device.description: True for the device that made the request, when it sent `X-Relic-Device`.

sessions_revoked.description: Whether every session on the account was actually signed out.

blob.description: Sealed, base64. Opaque to the server.

url.description: The link without the key. The client appends `#<key>`.

source.description: Which upgrade button opened this checkout. Recorded on the Stripe session when it is one of the known tags; anything else is dropped and the checkout still goes through.
